ai.description: Blythia hmuifang reaches a snout-vent length of 316 mm. It is dark brown dorsally with a yellow-orange venter and a distinct, broad yellow nuchal collar. A diagnostic feature is the single internasal.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Blythia hmuifang* is uniquely distinguished by its uniform, glossy dark-brown to blackish dorsal coloration, which lacks the distinct pale nuchal collar found in other *Blythia* species.
ai.habitat: *Blythia hmuifang* inhabits high-altitude subtropical broadleaf forests in Mizoram, India, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 1,600 meters.
ai.behavior: *Blythia hmuifang* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage through leaf litter and soil in search of earthworms and other small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Blythia hmuifang* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding details remain limited, it is believed to reproduce during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Blythia hmuifang* is endemic to the state of Mizoram in Northeast India, where it has been recorded at elevations around 1,500 meters within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
